| Engine piece | Home | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Checks runner + hooks | [`checks/`](engine/checks/README.md) | the dependency-free runner, its lib, the Stop hook, the PreToolUse guard — runs the packs' checks; owns no rule itself |
| Pack discovery + prose injection | `engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs`, `engine/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.mjs` | structural scan of `packs/*/pack.mjs`; SessionStart injection of active packs' prose |
| Skill mounting | `engine/pack_loader/mount-skills.mjs` | per-session symlink of the active packs' bundled-skill union (`<pack>/skills/<name>/`) |
| Adoption interviews | `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/interview.mjs` | the gap computation (a pack's declared questions minus the entry's stored answers) and the SessionStart nudge; owns no question itself — bundled in the adoption skill, resolved fail-soft by the engine |
| Baseline-migration mechanism | [`engine/migrations/`](engine/migrations/README.md) | the read-side resolver and write-side rename for a relocation; a record lives under the flow that owns it (the engine's, or `packs/<pack>/migrations/`), records are kept forever, and vendoring's 7-day recency window decides what ships to consumers |
| The task scheduler | [`engine/scheduler/`](docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md) | in each repo's own workflow: discovers its active packs' `tasks/<name>/task.mjs`, intersects them with the due slots, collects signals, runs each precondition, dispatches; pack-agnostic, owns no task, depends on no pack |
| The executor | [`engine/scheduler/executor.md`](engine/scheduler/executor.md) | the label-fired agent side of the scheduler — claims one dispatch issue, runs its task's worker against its own repo, delivers at the task's outcome ceiling |
| Bootstrap / baselining | [`bootstrap.md`](bootstrap.md), `engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --init` | adoption and the idempotent per-repo re-run |

...
| **Contributed config** | `contributes: { <pack>: ... }` | configuration addressed to another (required) pack — a fixed folder-barrier is the canonical case. The target pack interprets its active contributors' data via its own `contributedRules(activePacks)` seam, returning first-class rules; the runner wires the two together, so composition is declaration + data, never a cross-pack import |

**Packs are independent.** A pack's code imports only its **own** files and the engine surface
(`checks/`, `mount/`, the machinery `.mjs` at the `packs/`/`skills/` roots) — never another
pack's code, and never a canon-internal tree (`vendoring/`): the vendor set ships
a pack only when declared and ships no canon-internal tree at all, so such an import crashes
every consumer that vendors the importer without its target. A pack that wants another pack's
*abilities* declares the dependency (`requires`) and passes **configuration**; a helper both

cat > updates/README.md <<'EOF'
# `updates/` — the flows that move a repo between versions

Canon-internal machinery (never vendored, like [`vendoring/`](../vendoring/README.md)): one runner
per **flow**, each moving a repo from the versions it has installed to the ones this canon tree
ships. The design — why the corpus splits into a versioned engine and versioned packs, and what
each flow may and may not do — is [`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md`](../docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md);
the release discipline the engine's versions follow is [`engine/RELEASES.md`](../engine/RELEASES.md).

| File | Flow |
|---|---|
| [`engine-update.mjs`](engine-update.mjs) | The **engine update**: replace the mount's engine wholesale, run the engine migrations in the repo's gap, converge the non-workflow wiring, stamp the new version. Deterministic end to end — no agentic stage, and no lane to add one. |

A runner here **judges everything before it writes anything**: a refused update leaves the repo
running exactly what it was running, which is the same transactional contract the vendor writer
keeps. Where it cannot proceed it returns a `needs-human` outcome naming what a person has to do —
it never half-applies, and it never quietly skips the step it could not take.

These run **from a canon checkout against a target repo**, like vendoring: updating is done *on* a
project, never *by* it.
EOF

input.title: Versioned updates Phase 1: the engine update flow
input.head: claude/claudinite-issue-768-g2qga2
input.body:
The engine updater box of #768. **Nothing calls it yet** — delivery, the selftest gate and auto-merge are the next boxes, so no member's converge changes on this PR.

## The flow

`updates/engine-update.mjs` moves one repo from the engine version it has installed to the one this canon ships:

1. **Replace** the mount's engine wholesale — the engine's own files never migrate, they are overwritten, so a half-applied engine cannot exist.
2. **Run** the engine migrations in the repo's gap — the records that repair *member-owned* files referencing engine surfaces.
3. **Converge** the non-workflow wiring, then **stamp** the new version.

The order is load-bearing: a record is written against the engine it lands with, so it must run on a mount that already holds that engine, and the stamp goes last because it is the claim that everything before it happened.

Two prohibitions hold by construction rather than by discipline:

- **No `.github/workflows/`.** `convergeWiring` gains a `workflows: false` option that this flow passes, and the materialize op already refuses a workflow dest unless the caller announces it can withhold — which this flow never does (it passes `env: {}`, because the handshake is a claim about the *running* process). Workflow churn is the pack flow's, per your decision.
- **No agentic work, ever.** An engine record carrying an `agentic` note ends the run at `needs-human` *before any write*, rather than being skipped quietly or handed to a model this flow cannot invoke.

Transactional throughout: everything judgeable is judged before the first byte, so a refused update leaves the repo running exactly the engine it was running.

## What the tests found

That agentic terminal is not theoretical. **Two engine records still carry notes** — `pack-independence` and `prework-rename` — so a repo below engine version 1 genuinely cannot be served by this flow yet. The test asserts the refusal against the real corpus instead of a fixture that would have hidden it, and the practical impact is nil once every member stamps engine 1 on its next converge. Converting those two notes is Phase 4's box, and I've noted on the issue that it now *gates* serving a lagging repo rather than being cleanup.

That is also why the registry-level "no `agentic:` on an engine migration" validator is **not** in this PR: a validator that rejects records the canon itself ships would be broken on arrival. The invariant is enforced where it bites — at the flow — and the schema-level throw belongs with Phase 4's conversion.

## Tests

Driven against **real member trees** built by the real vendor writer, not a fixture corpus — a fixture would prove the sequencing and say nothing about whether this canon's engine can actually be laid down on a repo. Ten cases: the engine/pack split of the file set, the gap emptying as a repo catches up, both refusal terminals writing nothing at all, wholesale replacement reverting local drift and dropping files the new engine no longer has, the packs half of the mount left untouched, no workflow written while the hooks it *may* converge still are, and a dry run that judges everything and writes nothing.

## New tree

`updates/` joins `vendoring/` as canon-internal machinery, never vendored — it will hold the pack updater and the install runner as Phases 2 and 3 land. Documented in `updates/README.md` and in `extending.md`'s engine map. Its file-placement advisories are accepted with a reason: an update flow *is* the composition of the trees it moves between, so every import it has crosses a boundary; putting it inside any one of them would either ship canon-internal machinery to every member or hide the flow inside the thing it operates on.

## Verification

1482 tests green, `selftest --strict` green, work checks clean, and the world advisory list identical to `origin/main` once the `updates/` accept is in.

Refs #768
